The guide no longer justifies the main allocation. Its strongest internally consistent version retains an intact partner map and restores registered contacts. That remains useful, but I have not identified a consequential operation that the matched keyed-carrier construction cannot also supply. I have therefore preserved the guide result and moved into a broader question: what determines whether mechanical loading preserves a dynamic network’s connections or accelerates their replacement?

This attack produced two substantive results. First, a chemically explicit ring-forming connector has competing exchange pathways that can defeat its intended force selectivity. Second, a common polymer model admits populations with identical elastic response and identical initial reaction rate, but opposite changes in reaction rate under deformation. The second result is the stronger foundation to retain.

Why the guide does not win its generous comparison

I granted favourable axial mobility while retaining the actual requirements: capped confinement, finite travel, registration, carrier packing, intact inventory, and the adhesive potential’s normal forces.

Under those conditions, the guide supplies three operations already established in our construction:

It retains the correspondence between carriers and partners.
Its geometry excludes wrong contacts within the proved clearance and reserve conditions.
It admits the aligned completion path.

Those results survive. So do the pose-induced normal load and the failures associated with attraction, crowding and constrained mobility. The assumed 25 mV surface potential, Hamaker sensitivity and guide clearances remain assumptions of that physical model.

The matched carrier bank can preserve the same correspondence using explicit keys, stops and finite travel. Shared travel could still improve a particular implementation’s packing or compliance, but we have not acquired a decisive advantage in footprint, retained load, repair range or recoverable damage. Nor does the guide recover missing carriers, reconstruct a destroyed reference, or write a new partner map.

That is an allocation judgment, not a universal cost equivalence. The bank must pay for its own registration and travel; the earlier separate-link optimum is not a global floor. But favourable guide mobility alone does not open a sufficiently different capability.

The stronger material operation I tested

The target was rapid exchange in damaged or unloaded material while loaded connections remain comparatively stable, without a permanent load-bearing skeleton or a global switch into a repair state.

The conventional alternatives set a demanding standard:

Independently effective alternative	What it already supplies
Catch-bond actin networks	Redistribution toward stressed regions can strengthen a network despite weaker individual bonds.
Permanent/dynamic silicone architectures	A permanent elastic component restores contact while a dynamic component heals, combining creep resistance with autonomous repair.
Associatively exchanging polymer networks	Connectivity can reorganize without requiring complete dissociation of every crosslink.

Mulla and colleagues already demonstrated the first mechanism. Menasce and colleagues demonstrated the second, including approximately 90% strength recovery after 24 hours for their bilayer test; the permanent component remained available to restore contact. These are substantial incumbents, not merely conceptual comparators.

+1

Ring-forming catch networks are also already a published simulation direction. The relevant 2026 preprint explicitly studies force-dependent suppression of ring formation and its network consequences. Its reaction implementation uses different opening and closing probabilities and capture distances, selected to preserve network integrity. Those rules define a computational mechanism; they do not measure the chemical selectivity of the connector below.

The intended cycle is chemically explicit:

The pendant thiol attacks its own thioester.
An A-tethered macrothiolactone forms, releasing B–SH.
Another B′–SH opens the ring, producing a connection to B′.

Tension can suppress step 1 by making the intramolecular encounter less probable. The same spacer that carries force supplies the encounter geometry. This avoids inserting a desired force-dependent rate by hand.

However, B′–SH can also attack the intact linear thioester directly. More consequentially, every intact connector already carries a pendant thiol. Pendants on other connectors can participate in intermolecular exchange even without added repair reagent. Such reactions can also move the system outside the intended family of independent connector cassettes.

Direct thiol–thioester exchange is established chemistry, including in stress-relaxing polymer networks. Its dependence on catalyst, solvent and functional-group identity is experimentally documented. It cannot be omitted simply because the intramolecular route is mechanically attractive.

This is not a universal ceiling. Steric exclusion, differing electrophile reactivity, spatial correlations and catalyst localization can change it. But those become the required construction. Published chemistry supplies relevant ingredients, but not that intersection. Their productive native chemical ligation also proceeds to an amide, changing the reversibility of the operation. This is the branch worth sustaining: determine which internal distributions and chemical reaction classes can remain useful while connections exchange. The present calculation supplies a concrete constitutive counterexample, a chemical-selectivity budget and a common-force test of a candidate. It does not yet supply durable memory: exchange can alter the distribution that encodes the response, and intermolecular attack can alter the intended connector class.

I am retaining the pendant-ring chemistry conditionally, with those failures explicit. Ciarella and colleagues found roughly an order-of-magnitude difference in network stress relaxation at similar exchange rates when the allowed topology differed. Reaction counts cannot simply be relabelled as material failure. arxiv.org

That is a constructive constraint on inverse design: the desired load response must be generated by an admissible conformation distribution and its associated forces. It cannot be freely specified as a rate function.

This is the branch worth sustaining: determine which internal distributions and chemical reaction classes can remain useful while connections exchange. The present calculation supplies a concrete constitutive counterexample, a chemical-selectivity budget and a common-force test of a candidate. It does not yet supply durable memory: exchange can alter the distribution that encodes the response, and intermolecular attack can alter the intended connector class.

I am retaining the pendant-ring chemistry conditionally, with those failures explicit. The next molecular advance must control the competing reactions and preserve the relevant internal state through exchange. Generic catch strengthening, another isolated ring-closing improvement, or favourable guide mobility would not by themselves meet that requirement.
